name: Rails ActiveRecord SQL String Interpolation
attack_scenario: Attacker submits email=' OR '1'='1' --; the interpolated fragment turns a single-row lookup into a full-table dump or auth bypass.
negative_test_hint: submit email "' OR '1'='1' --" and assert the lookup returns a single row or errors instead of bypassing authentication

exemplar.compliant: User.where("email = ?", params[:email]).order(sort_column)  # sort_column validated against an allowlist
exemplar.explanation: ActiveRecord where/order/find_by_sql accept raw SQL fragments; interpolating (#{...}) or concatenating (+) any value into that string reopens SQL injection despite the ORM. Bind parameters (?, named binds) keep values out of the SQL grammar, and column/direction names must come from an allowlist.
